data.name: Disney Infinity 3.0: Gold Edition
data.detailed_description:
Disney Infinity 3.0: Gold Edition includes Star Wars™ to the ever-growing collection of Marvel, Disney and Disney•Pixar characters, stories and worlds NOW with all Disney Infinity Characters and Playsets Unlocked. Together new heroes can join forces with all other Disney Infinity characters and embark on adventures as big as your imagination in the 3.0 Toy Box! Disney Infinity encourages you to play your way, whether you explore open-world creation in the Toy Box or story-driven gameplay inside Play Sets!

All Disney Infinity 3.0 Playsets Unlocked:
- Twilight of the Republic
- Rise Against the Empire
- The Force Awakens
- And More...

All Disney Infinity 3.0 Characters Unlocked:
- Rey
- Yoda
- Chewbacca
- Han Solo
- Darth Vader
- Hulkbuster
- Ultron
- Iron Man
- Olaf
- All Disney Infinity 1.0 Characters
- All Disney Infinity 2.0 Characters
- And More...

Enjoy Disney Infinity with a Full Toy Box!

reviews.review:
Disney Infinity, in hindsight, is probably the type of game that should have been futureproof, both in concept and in content.  The idea that Disney, who produces several films across a variety of genres for all ages, had a game that was the ultimate sandbox that could produce easy content on top of custom maps created by users, meant to be played literally for infinity.  Unfortunately, they just didn't want to stay in the "toys to life" model and ultimately dropped the games entirely.  Shame, really.  I've always felt this was a solid logical step towards movie tie-ins as it's allows development of small scale levels be built around the toys they release over time to promote and... well I have my ideas that I'll keep to myself here as I ultimately do not know everything that happened behind the scenes.  There is a lot of potential wasted here in hindsight.

What we have here though is a game that is, by all accounts, the ultimate game to play within the Disney space circa 2017.  A mashup of several Disney, Marvel, and Star Wars properties cobbled together for a sandbox experience.  There are a few built in levels that give players the general concept of what could possibly be built and then allow the player to essentially "build" their own game with the tools present.  It is quite the experience to see the various properties interact for a time long before Fortnite became the beast it is now at the time of writing.  The idea of Luke Skywalker running about with Buzz Lightyear  while Captain America fends off villains is a fever dream of sorts.  It's shame there is no co-op play like the original games included, even if utilizing the workarounds.  This is a game where, eventually, you have to make your own fun in a single player space, something that is still quite possible.

Years ago, there was a community surrounding this game that was crafting unique adventures within the spaces this game has.  A lot of that is now lost to time, sadly, as that community faded away to other projects and games.

It is recommended if not only for the experience of all the various versions of this game but for the novelty of what these games presented: a metaverse of Disney properties before it was cool.
